products.note: Green, forested, and distinctive -- one of the defining Japanese single malts. Superb, and priced accordingly.
The benchmark Japanese single malt. Consistently excellent, and the price reflects genuine, sustained demand rather than hype.
Same benchmark Yamazaki 12 Year inside a limited-edition package. Excellent whisky, collector pricing.
An iconic, beautifully balanced blend in one of the most recognizable bottles in whisky. Worth it whenever it is not marked up for scarcity.
Nikka's smokier, coastal single malt. Distinctive and highly regarded among Japanese whisky drinkers.
The same excellent Harmony liquid in commemorative packaging. Buy it for the whisky, not the box.
Punchy, rich, remarkably complete. The best-value Japanese bottle here.
No age statement, but this is the most accessible way onto the legendary Yamazaki name. Genuinely excellent.
Nikka's fruitier, more floral single malt (as opposed to Yoichi's smokier profile). Excellent and well-regarded.
Mizunara-cask finished single malt. Distinctive sandalwood-and-coconut character from the Japanese oak.
Taiwanese, not Japanese, despite the shelf placement -- but genuinely excellent. Tropical-climate aging gives it fast, fruit-forward maturity.
Sweet, vanilla, unusual. Very good neat, if you can justify seventy dollars.
Malted barley run through a Coffey still -- a genuinely distinct texture from a traditional pot-still single malt.
Kaiyo's mizunara character at full proof. More intense and structured than their standard bottling.
A smokier, more assertive variant of standard Toki. Worth the small step up if you find Toki thin.

products.n: Hatozaki Finest Blended Whiskey With Glass
products.note: A well-regarded budget-premium Japanese blend. Balanced and easy-drinking.
Kaiyo's standard bottling. The mizunara oak character comes through clearly.
A step up from Hatozaki's Finest bottle. More balanced and complex.
Nikka's blended-malt bottle, the black-label version. Solid and well-liked.
An approachable, budget-friendly rice-forward blend. A fair entry point into Japanese whisky.
Aged across five cask types including mizunara oak. Young but genuinely interesting for the price.
Light and clean. Built for highballs, priced above its weight.
Rice whisky rather than malt or grain in the Scotch sense. Smooth and mixable, a different lane entirely.
A blend across five whisky-producing nations -- an interesting concept that is decent rather than exceptional in the glass.
Finished with a touch of sake and umeshu influence. Distinctive, though the flavor is more novelty than classic whisky.

products.n: Hatozaki Sm Batch Whisky 12 Yr Umeshu Cask Finish
products.note: Plum-wine cask finish gives it a sweet, unusual profile. A novelty pour more than a classic sipping whisky.
Mars Shinshu's entry-level blend. A decent budget option, less refined than the bigger names.
Higher proof than the standard Iwai. More backbone, still an entry-level blend.
A budget blend with mixed reception. Fine for the price, not a category standout.
A novelty collector bottle riding the Godzilla branding. The packaging premium far outweighs what is in the glass.

products.n: The Last Drop R39 Japanese Whiskey 22 YO
